headline: Highest risk is medium: Flowise’s broad filesystem/network access can feed next-ai-draw-io untrusted content, but no direct shared-channel or compliance breach is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while next-ai-draw-io ingests files and supports MCP and browser-based AI workflows. A shared workspace or file handoff could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same uploaded file directory or workspace, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF next-ai-draw-io parses Flowise-generated text or diagrams as instructions, the attack path is active.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories or buckets.
Disable automatic ingestion of files produced by the other agent.
Require a human review step before any file is re-opened as instructions.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and content-sanitization gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and stores files on the server filesystem; next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and can send data to multiple external model APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive content can flow from Flowise into next-ai-draw-io and then to third-party inference backends. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem or uploaded-document store, leakage risk is active.
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use a hosted model API, file contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace.
Route next-ai-draw-io to a local model only.
Turn off automatic file re-upload between tools.
Restrict Flowise outputs to redacted summaries.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has broad filesystem write access and shared state via server datastore; next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and can use MCP plus external APIs. If both operate on the same mutable files or environment variables, they can overwrite each other’s artifacts or credentials. No locking mechanism is documented, so the overlap is a real default-deployment conflict.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF both agents mutate shared environment variables or secrets, one can break the other’s run.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Store secrets in per-agent secret stores.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-run lock file.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same diagrams or flow definitions.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces chatflow outputs and can call tools; next-ai-draw-io turns natural-language commands into AI-assisted visualization and can use MCP/model APIs. That creates a plausible chain where Flowise output becomes next-ai-draw-io input without verification, causing incorrect diagrams or actions to propagate. Because the pair is not directly documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Flowise output is pasted or piped into next-ai-draw-io without review, errors can cascade.
IF next-ai-draw-io treats Flowise-generated text as authoritative, downstream diagrams may encode false facts.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require source citations before diagram generation.
Use a checklist to validate key facts.
Limit Flowise to drafting only, not final instructions.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the evidence does not show a specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets; next-ai-draw-io handles documents and API keys, but no PHI/EU-only data class or policy conflict is documented. The other agent is cited because the compliance question is pairwise, yet the current evidence only supports a low, gap-based concern.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into both tools, policy review is required.
IF either deployment routes data to a region with stricter residency rules, a mismatch may emerge.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before use.
Keep regulated data out of both tools unless approved.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Prefer local models for sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
